_comment: College, Career, and Civic Life (C3) Framework Social Studies Alignment Data
_description: Contains grade-by-grade Social Studies standards across Civics (D2.Civ), Economics (D2.Eco), Geography (D2.Geo), and History (D2.His).

social.name: Social Studies
social.desc: Inquiry into human societies, civic engagement, global geography, economics, and world history aligned to the C3 Framework.

ccss.title: Pre-K Self, Family, & Community Foundations
ccss.overview: Developing foundational awareness of self, family traditions, classroom rules, community helpers, and spatial awareness within the school environment.
ccss.standards:
Civic Ideals & Classroom Citizenship (PK.C3.Civ)

PK.Civ.1: Understand and follow simple classroom and family rules, demonstrating fairness and turn-taking.

PK.Civ.2: Identify community helpers (firefighters, doctors, mail carriers, teachers) and their roles.

Geography: Spatial Awareness (PK.C3.Geo)

PK.Geo.1: Use spatial terms (near, far, up, down, inside, outside) to describe physical locations in the school and home.

Economics: Needs and Wants (PK.C3.Eco)

PK.Eco.1: Distinguish between basic needs (food, water, shelter) and wants (toys, treats).
competencies: Demonstrate fair play and follow shared group rules
Recognize roles of community helpers
Use spatial vocabulary to describe locations
Differentiate between basic needs and wants

ccss.title: Kindergarten Social Studies: Being a Good Citizen (C3)
ccss.overview: Learning what it means to be a responsible citizen in a community, understanding the purpose of rules and laws, using basic maps, and exploring national symbols and holidays.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Rules, Rights, and Responsibilities (D2.Civ.K)

D2.Civ.1.K-2: Describe how people benefit from and are challenged by working together, including through government, workplace, voluntary organizations, and families.

D2.Civ.3.K-2: Explain the need for and purposes of rules in various settings, inside and outside of school.

D2.Civ.7.K-2: Apply civic virtues (e.g., honesty, mutual respect, cooperation) when participating in school settings.

Geography: Maps and Places (D2.Geo.K)

D2.Geo.1.K-2: Construct maps, graphs, and other representations of familiar places (e.g., classroom, bedroom, neighborhood).

D2.Geo.3.K-2: Use location terms and geographic representations to describe places and environmental characteristics.

Economics: Goods, Services, and Scarcity (D2.Eco.K)

D2.Eco.1.K-2: Explain how scarcity necessitates decision making and choices.

D2.Eco.2.K-2: Identify the goods and services that people produce and those that are produced in other communities.

History: Change Over Time & Heritage (D2.His.K)

D2.His.1.K-2: Create a chronological sequence of events in their own lives and families.

D2.His.3.K-2: Generate questions about individuals and groups who have shaped significant historical events and national holidays.
competencies: Explain purposes of laws and civic responsibilities
Draw and interpret basic maps of familiar spaces
Identify choices made due to economic scarcity
Order personal and historical events chronologically

ccss.title: 1st Grade Social Studies: Families, Culture, & Neighborhoods (C3)
ccss.overview: Investigating family histories, diverse cultural traditions, local neighborhood geography, basic trade and money, and democratic decision-making through voting.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Democratic Participation (D2.Civ.1)

D2.Civ.2.K-2: Explain how all people, not just official leaders, play important roles in a community.

D2.Civ.14.K-2: Describe how groups of people make decisions to promote the common good (e.g., voting and consensus).

Geography: Neighborhood Landscapes & Globes (D2.Geo.1)

D2.Geo.2.K-2: Use maps, globes, and other simple geographic models to identify land and water features (continents and oceans).

D2.Geo.7.K-2: Explain how people modify and adapt to their physical environment (shelters, clothing, transportation).

Economics: Work, Earning, and Saving (D2.Eco.1)

D2.Eco.4.K-2: Describe the goods and services that people produce and why people trade with one another using money.

D2.Eco.6.K-2: Explain how people save money for future goods and services.
competencies: Describe democratic voting and community decision making
Identify continents, oceans, and landforms on globes
Explain how human choices adapt to physical environments
Understand earning, spending, trading, and saving money

ccss.title: 2nd Grade Social Studies: Global Communities & Local Government (C3)
ccss.overview: Understanding local and municipal government structures, mayors and town councils, world geography, comparing diverse cultures, and producers/consumers in the local economy.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Government and Community Leadership (D2.Civ.2)

D2.Civ.5.K-2: Explain what governments are and some of their key functions (e.g., public safety, parks, schools, roads).

D2.Civ.6.K-2: Describe how people choose leaders through elections in local government.

Geography: Human Settlement & Spatial Interaction (D2.Geo.2)

D2.Geo.6.K-2: Identify cultural and environmental characteristics of different communities and nations around the world.

D2.Geo.8.K-2: Compare how people in different places use natural resources to meet their needs.

Economics: Producers and Consumers (D2.Eco.2)

D2.Eco.9.K-2: Describe the role of banks and financial institutions in saving and investing.

D2.Eco.12.K-2: Describe how specialized workers produce goods that are traded regionally and globally.
competencies: Explain functions of local town councils, mayors, and municipal services
Compare global cultural traditions and geographic adaptations
Distinguish between producer and consumer roles
Analyze how natural resources shape regional economies

ccss.title: 3rd Grade Social Studies: Regional Cultures & World Geography (C3)
ccss.overview: Deep inquiry into indigenous cultures, early settlement patterns, geographic regions, human interaction with environment, and basic principles of supply and demand.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Civic Participation & Deliberation (D2.Civ.3)

D2.Civ.8.3-5: Identify core civic virtues and democratic principles that guide government and citizen actions.

D2.Civ.10.3-5: Identify the beliefs, experiences, perspectives, and values that underlie points of view on public issues.

Geography: Regions, Resources, and Maps (D2.Geo.3)

D2.Geo.2.3-5: Use maps, satellite images, photographs, and other representations to explain relationships between the locations of places and regions.

D2.Geo.5.3-5: Explain how the cultural and environmental characteristics of places change over time.

Economics: Markets, Supply, and Demand (D2.Eco.3)

D2.Eco.3.3-5: Identify examples of the variety of resources (human, capital, and natural) that are used to produce goods and services.

D2.Eco.6.3-5: Explain how pricing influences the decisions of buyers and sellers in competitive markets.

History: Indigenous Peoples & Settlement (D2.His.3)

D2.His.2.3-5: Compare life in specific historical periods with life today, focusing on indigenous nations and early settlers.
competencies: Analyze diverse viewpoints on civic community issues
Interpret topographic, political, and thematic regional maps
Identify human, natural, and capital resources in economic production
Examine history and cultural heritage of indigenous peoples

ccss.title: 4th Grade Social Studies: State History & Physical Geography (C3)
ccss.overview: In-depth exploration of state history, colonial expansion, frontier migrations, state government, industrial innovations, and conservation of natural resources.
ccss.standards:
Civics: State Government & Constitution (D2.Civ.4)

D2.Civ.5.3-5: Explain the origins, functions, and structure of state government (executive, legislative, judicial branches).

D2.Civ.6.3-5: Describe ways in which people benefit from and are challenged by state laws and public policies.

Geography: State Regions & Physical Systems (D2.Geo.4)

D2.Geo.4.3-5: Explain how culture influences the way people modify and adapt to their environments in different state regions.

D2.Geo.9.3-5: Analyze the effects of catastrophic environmental events on human populations and settlement patterns.

History: State Exploration, Colonization, and Growth (D2.His.4)

D2.His.3.3-5: Generate questions about individuals and groups who have shaped significant historical events in state development.

D2.His.14.3-5: Explain probable causes and effects of events and developments in state history (railroads, agriculture, urbanization).
competencies: Analyze the three branches of state government and the state constitution
Evaluate human environmental modification and conservation efforts
Examine primary and secondary sources in state historical archives
Trace cause-and-effect relationships in economic and industrial growth

ccss.title: 5th Grade Social Studies: Early United States History (C3)
ccss.overview: United States history from pre-Columbian eras through the American Revolution, the drafting of the U.S. Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and early westward expansion.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Principles of the U.S. Constitution (D2.Civ.5)

D2.Civ.3.3-5: Examine the origins and purposes of the Declaration of Independence, the U.S. Constitution, and the Bill of Rights.

D2.Civ.4.3-5: Explain how the U.S. Constitution protects individual freedoms and rights and establishes checks and balances.

Geography: North American Exploration & Territories (D2.Geo.5)

D2.Geo.7.3-5: Explain how physical and cultural characteristics of places in North America influenced the movement of people, goods, and ideas.

History: Colonization, Revolution, & New Nation (D2.His.5)

D2.His.1.3-5: Create and use chronological timelines to plot key events leading to the American Revolutionary War.

D2.His.9.3-5: Summarize the differing perspectives of Loyalists, Patriots, enslaved individuals, and Native Americans during the American Revolution.

D2.His.16.3-5: Use evidence to develop a claim about the past regarding early constitutional debates.
competencies: Analyze foundational civic texts: Declaration of Independence & Constitution
Explain checks and balances, separation of powers, and the Bill of Rights
Evaluate multiple perspectives on the American Revolutionary War
Synthesize historical evidence to evaluate early American governance

ccss.title: 6th Grade Social Studies: Ancient World Civilizations (C3)
ccss.overview: Comprehensive world history from the Neolithic revolution through river valley civilizations (Mesopotamia, Egypt, Indus Valley, Yellow River), Classical Greece, Rome, and Silk Road trade networks.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Origins of Governance & Legal Codes (D2.Civ.6)

D2.Civ.1.6-8: Distinguish the powers and responsibilities of citizens, political leaders, and military rulers in ancient city-states (Hammurabi's Code, Athenian Democracy, Roman Republic).

D2.Civ.3.6-8: Examine the origins, purposes, and impact of constitutions, treaties, and law codes in classical antiquity.

Geography: River Valleys & Trade Corridors (D2.Geo.6)

D2.Geo.4.6-8: Explain how cultural patterns and economic decisions shaped the development of agricultural river basins (Tigris, Euphrates, Nile, Indus, Yangtze).

D2.Geo.7.6-8: Analyze the environmental factors that facilitated ancient trade networks, such as the Silk Roads and Mediterranean maritime routes.

History: Classical Philosophy, Innovation, and Decline (D2.His.6)

D2.His.1.6-8: Analyze connections between ancient philosophical traditions (Confucianism, Buddhism, Greek philosophy) and civic organization.

D2.His.14.6-8: Explain multiple causes and effects of the rise, expansion, and collapse of classical empires.
competencies: Compare early legal and political systems: Hammurabi to Athenian Democracy
Evaluate geographic factors essential to agricultural surplus and civilization
Analyze cultural diffusion across Afro-Eurasian trade routes
Examine technological, philosophical, and architectural innovations of antiquity

ccss.title: 7th Grade Social Studies: Medieval History & Global Encounters (C3)
ccss.overview: Medieval Europe, Islamic Golden Age, Sub-Saharan African empires (Ghana, Mali), imperial China, feudal Japan, Mayan/Incan civilizations, and the global age of exploration.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Feudalism, Theocracies, and Empires (D2.Civ.7)

D2.Civ.4.6-8: Explain the relationships between social hierarchies, feudal contracts, and central authority in medieval Eurasia.

D2.Civ.13.6-8: Analyze the Magna Carta and the emergence of limited government and parliamentary institutions.

Geography: Trans-Saharan & Maritime Diffusion (D2.Geo.7)

D2.Geo.8.6-8: Analyze how human modifications to geographic landscapes influenced cultural exchange in medieval trading cities (Timbuktu, Baghdad, Venice, Chang'an).

D2.Geo.11.6-8: Explain how navigation innovations (astrolabe, compass, caravel) enabled oceanic global exchange.

History: The Renaissance, Reformation, and Colombian Exchange (D2.His.7)

D2.His.2.6-8: Classify series of historical events and developments as examples of change and/or continuity over time (Renaissance humanism, scientific revolution).

D2.His.15.6-8: Evaluate the profound demographic and ecological consequences of the Columbian Exchange across the Americas, Africa, and Europe.
competencies: Trace historical emergence of constitutional constraints: Magna Carta (1215)
Analyze scholastic and scientific innovations during the Islamic Golden Age
Examine cultural and mercantile strength of West African empires
Evaluate social, ecological, and economic impacts of the Columbian Exchange

ccss.title: 8th Grade Social Studies: U.S. History from Revolution to Reconstruction (C3)
ccss.overview: Rigorous study of American history from the Constitutional Convention through Westward Expansion, the antebellum reform movements, the Civil War, and Reconstruction.
ccss.standards:
Civics: Federalism and the Constitutional Republic (D2.Civ.8)

D2.Civ.6.6-8: Describe the roles of political parties, interest groups, and media in influencing public policy in the early republic.

D2.Civ.8.6-8: Analyze judicial review and landmark Supreme Court decisions (Marbury v. Madison, McCulloch v. Maryland, Dred Scott v. Sandford).

Economics: Sectionalism & Industrialization (D2.Eco.8)

D2.Eco.7.6-8: Analyze how technological innovations (cotton gin, steam engines, canals) produced diverging economic systems in the North and South.

D2.Eco.8.6-8: Explain the institutional economic foundation of slavery and its pervasive national impact.

History: Civil War, Abolition, and Reconstruction Amendments (D2.His.8)

D2.His.4.6-8: Analyze multiple factors that influenced the perspectives of people during the abolitionist movement, women's suffrage, and secession crisis.

D2.His.14.6-8: Explain the strategic, human, and ideological dimensions of the Civil War (Gettysburg, Emancipation Proclamation).

D2.His.16.6-8: Evaluate the successes and failures of Reconstruction, including the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments and the rise of Jim Crow laws.
competencies: Evaluate Constitutional federalism, judicial review, and sectional crises
Analyze economic divergences: Northern industrialization vs. Southern agrarian slavery
Examine abolitionist rhetoric, speeches, and primary historical documents
Assess the legal and social impact of the Reconstruction Amendments

ccss.title: High School Social Studies: U.S. Government, Economics, & Modern World (C3)
ccss.overview: Advanced inquiry into American democratic institutions, macroeconomics, international relations, modern global conflicts, human rights declarations, and contemporary civic participation.
ccss.standards:
U.S. Government & Constitutional Law (D2.Civ.9-12)

D2.Civ.2.9-12: Analyze the role of citizens in the U.S. political system, and evaluate the collateral effects of elections at national, state, and local levels.

D2.Civ.4.9-12: Explain how the U.S. Constitution grants and distributes power to government to achieve the common good while protecting individual rights.

D2.Civ.14.9-12: Analyze how judicial review shapes public policy and individual rights through Fourteenth Amendment Due Process and Equal Protection jurisprudence.

Macroeconomics & Global Markets (D2.Eco.9-12)

D2.Eco.1.9-12: Analyze how economic systems (market, command, mixed) answer foundational questions of production and distribution.

D2.Eco.6.9-12: Generate possible explanations for a government role in market failure, antitrust regulation, monetary policy (Federal Reserve), and fiscal policy.

Modern World & U.S. History (D2.His.9-12)

D2.His.1.9-12: Evaluate how historical events and developments were shaped by unique circumstances of time and place (World Wars, Cold War, Decolonization, Civil Rights Movement).

D2.His.16.9-12: Integrate evidence from multiple relevant historical sources and interpretations into a reasoned argument about past policy decisions.
competencies: Analyze Constitutional law, Federalism, and civil rights jurisprudence
Evaluate macroeconomic indicators (GDP, inflation, unemployment) and Federal Reserve policy
Synthesize multi-source historical archives on twentieth-century geopolitical conflicts
Formulate evidence-based policy briefs addressing complex civic dilemmas
